item.title: China boycotts top AI conference over US sanctions ban
item.description:
China's leading science organizations have announced a boycott of the world's premier artificial intelligence conference after it barred submissions from US-sanctioned entities, marking a sharp escalation in the technological rivalry between Washington and Beijing.

The China Association for Science and Technology (CAST), the country's largest federation for science and technology professionals, said on Friday that it would stop accepting funding applications for members wanting to attend the Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, known as NeurIPS, and would redirect researchers to domestic conferences or "international conferences that respect the rights and interests of Chinese academics," according to Reuters.

item.title: TUM team finds fix for perovskite solar cell weathering
item.description: A wave of new research from labs across Europe and Asia is tackling the biggest obstacle standing between perovskite solar cells and widespread commercial adoption: their tendency to degrade under real-world weather conditions. In parallel, new manufacturing ventures are pushing to slash production costs, bringing the next generation of solar technology closer to rooftops and industrial surfaces worldwide.

item.title: ECB survey shows Iran war upended eurozone inflation outlook
item.description: Consumer confidence across Europe and the United Kingdom has deteriorated sharply as the war in Iran sends energy prices higher and revives memories of the 2022 cost-of-living crisis, according to a wave of surveys released this week.

item.title: Study finds cells, firms and cities all slow in adding new functions as they grow
item.description: A mystery novel and a fantasy epic may have little in common, but count the words inside them and a pattern emerges: new vocabulary appears quickly at first, then tapers off as the author reuses what has already been introduced. A new study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences finds that the same mathematical rule governs how living cells, corporations, government agencies, and cities grow and diversify — and the implications stretch from biology to business strategy.

item.title: SpaceX eyes IPO filing as Shotwell lands TIME cover
item.description:
TIME has put SpaceX President and COO Gwynne Shotwell on its latest cover, casting the longtime executive as the operational center of a company that has grown beyond rockets into satellite internet, lunar systems and, now, artificial intelligence. The profile arrives weeks after SpaceX said it had acquired xAI, Elon Musk’s AI company, in a deal reported by Reuters and CNBC at a combined $$1.25$$ trillion-dollar valuation, and as Reuters reported this week that the company is aiming to file IPO paperwork with regulators soon.

The timing matters because the story TIME tells is not simply about a magazine cover. It is about whether Shotwell, one of the most influential executives in aerospace, can help steer a newly enlarged SpaceX through the risks of absorbing xAI while preparing for one of the most closely watched market debuts in years.

item.title: Kremlin denies Putin asked oligarchs to fund Ukraine war costs
item.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin convened a closed-door meeting with the country's wealthiest business leaders on Thursday and urged them to make direct financial contributions to the state budget, as the Kremlin struggles to sustain the mounting costs of its war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year.

The appeal, first reported by the Financial Times citing three people familiar with the discussions, marks the first time Putin has personally asked Russia's oligarchs for money to support defense expenditures. The independent Russian outlet The Bell published a similar account Thursday evening, also citing unnamed sources.

item.title: Asia-Pacific governments rush to calm markets as Middle East war drives energy crisis
item.description:
Governments across the Asia-Pacific are rolling out emergency fiscal packages, fuel subsidies, and liquidity injections as the war between the United States and Israel against Iran continues to rattle energy markets and erode economic confidence across the region.

A Reuters factbox published Friday catalogued the widening list of interventions, from emergency bond purchases in South Korea to crude oil futures intervention being weighed by Japan, as policymakers scramble to shield their economies from the fallout of a conflict now entering its second month.

item.title: Scientists train to dive beneath polar ice as warming accelerates Arctic research
item.description: From the frozen lakes of Arctic Finland to the vast ice sheets of Antarctica, researchers are pushing into some of Earth's least explored frontiers — the hidden worlds beneath polar ice — seeking to understand how climate change is reshaping these environments and what long-buried landscapes can reveal about the planet's past.

item.title: SpaceX IPO sparks $15M in ticker bets before filing
item.description: SpaceX has not yet filed its IPO paperwork, but traders and retail investors are already treating it like the market event of the decade. On prediction platform Polymarket, combined trading volume on bets related to the company's valuation, listing exchange, and ticker symbol surpassed $15.2 million as of Friday, according to Reuters. The frenzy underscores the extraordinary anticipation surrounding what could become the largest initial public offering in history.

item.title: Ukraine, Saudi Arabia sign defense deal during Zelensky's surprise visit
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky made a surprise visit to Saudi Arabia on Thursday and signed a defense cooperation agreement with the kingdom, marking a new chapter in Kyiv's efforts to trade its hard-won drone warfare expertise for the advanced weapons it needs to fend off Russia.

The deal, signed before Zelensky met with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Jeddah, lays the groundwork for future contracts, technological cooperation, and investments, according to Zelensky, who announced the agreement on social media. "Ukraine is ready for long-term and mutually beneficial cooperation," Zelensky wrote on X after meeting with Ukrainian military experts already stationed in the kingdom.

item.title: Rubio presses G7 allies on Iran as Europeans hold firm on Ukraine
item.description: Foreign ministers from the Group of Seven nations gathered at the Abbaye des Vaux-de-Cernay near Paris this week for two days of talks that laid bare a widening transatlantic divide, with the United States pushing its allies to back the war against Iran while European partners insisted on sustaining military support for Ukraine and tightening sanctions on Russia.

item.title: Deployed nuclear warheads rose again in 2025, report finds
item.description:
The number of nuclear weapons deployed and ready for use grew again in 2025, according to the annual Nuclear Weapons Ban Monitor released on March 26, underscoring what arms control experts called a dangerous trajectory at a time when the last remaining treaty limiting the world's two largest arsenals has lapsed.

The nine nuclear-armed states — the United States, Russia, the United Kingdom, France, China, India, Pakistan, North Korea, and Israel — possessed a combined 12,187 warheads at the start of 2026, with 9,745 of those available for military use, an increase of 141 from the previous year. Of that total, 4,012 warheads were deployed on ballistic missiles, submarines, or at bomber bases, a rise of 108 over 2024.

item.title: China launches two trade barrier probes against U.S.
item.description: China's Ministry of Commerce on Friday announced two trade barrier investigations targeting the United States, directly mirroring Washington's own Section 301 probes launched earlier this month and marking a sharp escalation in the trade friction between the world's two largest economies.

item.title: Iran halts two Chinese ships near Hormuz in rare reversal
item.description:
Two ultra-large container ships operated by China's state-owned COSCO Shipping attempted to exit the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz on Friday but abruptly reversed course near Iran's Larak Island, according to ship-tracking data and crew members stationed nearby.

The vessels — the CSCL Indian Ocean and the CSCL Arctic Ocean, each capable of carrying 19,000 twenty-foot equivalent units of cargo — executed U-turns at approximately 03:20 and 03:50 UTC, roughly 20 miles from the southern Iranian port of Bandar Abbas. The incident marked the first attempted crossing of the strait by a major container carrier since the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran began on February 28.

item.title: Wikipedia bans AI-generated articles on English site
item.description: English Wikipedia has officially prohibited the use of large language models to write or rewrite articles, a policy adopted on March 20 after volunteer editors voted overwhelmingly in favor of the restriction. The new guideline, which now appears on Wikipedia's content policy pages, states that "text generated by large language models often violates several of Wikipedia's core content policies" and that their use for generating or rewriting article content "is prohibited."

item.title: NeurIPS apologizes after China boycotts over sanctions ban
item.description:
China's largest science and technology organizations announced a boycott of NeurIPS, one of the world's most prestigious artificial intelligence conferences, after it barred submissions from entities on U.S. sanctions lists — a move that effectively locked out major Chinese tech firms including Huawei and SMIC. By Friday, NeurIPS organizers issued an apology, acknowledging they had overstepped their legal obligations.

The China Association for Science and Technology (CAST) said on Friday that it would immediately stop accepting funding applications from members seeking to attend NeurIPS and would redirect researchers toward domestic conferences or "international conferences that respect the rights and interests of Chinese academics," according to Reuters. Papers published at NeurIPS will no longer qualify as research outputs for CAST's funding programs.

item.title: Rubio says US expects Iran war to end in weeks
item.description:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio told G7 foreign ministers on Friday that the U.S. military operation against Iran is expected to conclude "in a matter of weeks, not months," offering the most specific timeline yet for the conflict now entering its fourth week. Speaking after meetings at the Vaux-de-Cernay Abbey near Paris, Rubio said all U.S. objectives could be achieved without ground troops and described the campaign as running ahead of schedule.

Rubio reportedly told ministers the war would last "two to four weeks" more, according to Axios, citing three unnamed sources. He also confirmed that indirect diplomatic contacts with Tehran were underway through intermediary countries, describing "some concrete progress," though he cautioned the situation remained fluid. "There are intermediary countries that are passing messages," Rubio told reporters before departing Washington. "That's an ongoing process".

item.title: Rubio calls Ukraine 'not America's war' as peace talks stall
item.description: As Russia launched the largest single-day drone assault of the war and pressed forward with a spring offensive, U.S.-mediated peace talks between Moscow, Kyiv, and Washington remain frozen with no new round scheduled — a diplomatic paralysis driven by the Trump administration's focus on the war in Iran.

item.title: Trump extends Iran deadline as energy crisis fuels renewables debate
item.description: Nearly a month after the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz upended global energy markets, a growing chorus of voices — from the head of the International Energy Agency to the United Nations Secretary-General — is arguing that the crisis should accelerate the world's shift toward renewable energy. The debate is intensifying even as the strait remains blocked and oil prices hover well above pre-war levels.

item.title: G7 agrees to multinational Hormuz escort mission after Iran war ends
item.description: Foreign ministers from the Group of Seven nations meeting outside Paris on Friday agreed to establish a multinational naval escort mission to reopen the Strait of Hormuz once the US-Israeli war against Iran concludes, marking the bloc's most concrete step yet toward addressing the waterway's near-total closure over the past month.
